notes: Handwritten French letter on squared paper, dated Bures sur Yvette, le 21 octobre 1968, addressed Cher Grothendieck. The supplied H description attributes the blue-ink letter to P. Deligne and the pencil note to Grothendieck; there is no signature on this sheet. The page states a criterion for a compact complex analytic space to be a scheme, reduces it to a square-zero extension, and writes a comparison diagram for algebraic and analytic extension groups. These are the author's claims; no proof verification was undertaken. The underlined word proposition is a local heading, not a separate document title. No manuscript page number, written sheet count, closing, or signature occurs. Archive number 74 is recorded only as a comment. The pencil note contains an authorial question mark after the ruled VI reference. Three original lexical/alphabet doubts (joindre, K versus blackboard K, and schéma) are retained. The uncertain marginal colon is represented by its observed diagonal pair of shapes. Pale isolated surface flecks inspected below Ext and beside the first label were not treated as authored mathematical signs. H has description only: all h_reading values are null and all diff_h values false.
math_reading_decisions: The criterion has X_{\mathrm{red}}: joined lowered red, without an added acute accent. The other point suffixes are small lowered ovals read as 0 in X_0.
The ideal is represented by \mathscr{N}: a rising left loop and a narrow tall stroke ending in a small loop recur in the prose and all formula arguments.
The extension-group E is an ordinary capital with a single upright and short horizontal arms. Its qualifiers an and alg are raised words, not subscripts.

The Hom and Ext initials have looped cursive forms, retained as \mathscr{H}om and \mathscr{E}xt; their following letters remain on the ordinary formula baseline. The Ext degrees are short raised single strokes, read as 1.
The first introduced K retains the explicit K versus \mathbb{K} doubt. The later K letters in parentheses show single stems and remain ordinary K.

The diagram retains H^{1^{\mathrm{alg}}} and H^{1^{\mathrm{an}}}, with the qualifiers on a second rise beside the degree. Its upper-right H has only the degree 0; the lower-right term is H^{0^{\mathrm{an}}}. No alg has been supplied to the upper-right term.

The diagram contains six rightward arrows and three downward arrows. The final horizontal arrow of the upper row is labelled \alpha; that of the lower row is labelled \beta. No terminal arrow after the rightmost object is present.
The earlier implication has two parallel shafts and a right-pointing head, retained as \Longrightarrow. The final inclusion is an open curved sign without an extra lower bar, retained as \subset.
The pencil numerals are VI and II, each with a separate upper and lower transverse rule. The two groups are retained with \overline{\underline{\mathrm{VI}}} and \overline{\underline{\mathrm{II}}}.
The first formula label is (1), and the diagram label is (2). The argument later refers to (1). These ink readings were retained; no numerical or mathematical reconstruction was used to add symbols.
